description: What enforces each controller rule (repo/CONTROLLER.md, its pages and the gate rules): a hook, a script, a CI check or the programme reconciler, each with the test that proves it and one line on which part of the rule it covers, or instruction-only with its basis (judgement, host-gap or planned) and reason. Each row holds rule_sha, the hash of its rule line, so an edited rule fails the check until its row is reviewed. Checked by repo/scripts/check-controller-enforcement-map.cjs.

rows.covers: Governance state decides on or off only from the merged programme file, and the governance hook holds work in a repository whose answer is not yet decided.

rows.rule: Bind one canonical repo, programme, release

instruction_only.why: Choosing the repository, release and one owning builder is a controller judgement; no code can tell which builder owns an outcome.

rows.covers: The merge hold refuses a merge without the owner's OK. The rest of the fence (binding the named repository, no cross-repository authority) is instruction-only.

instruction_only.why: Vetting feedback and choosing to extend, reopen or create a child stay a judgement; the Nearest child line on a new child is code-checkable.
instruction_only.planned: #1225 N1: a CHILD_NO_NEAREST finding checks the Nearest child line.

rows.rule: Keep in-flight gates on their admitted Controller revision

instruction_only.why: No launcher records the controller revision a gate was admitted on, so nothing can compare it.
instruction_only.planned: #1265 L4: assign records the CONTROLLER.md blob a gate was admitted on, and handover flags a changed blob.

rows.rule: Preserve every commitment, in flight or queued
rows.covers: The reconciler works out each child's group (in flight or queued) and sorts the queue in work order; it does not keep owners or commitments.

The reconciler raises TASK_IDLE and TASK_MERGED_OPEN for tasks in flight that nothing is moving, refuses to acknowledge them and lists them first, and keeps the QUEUED band in work order (priority, size S, all other work, marked last, dependencies held). Each task's priority and size are the controller's judgement.

instruction_only.why: Whether a fix is small and which slice it joins is a judgement made before any branch exists.
A test pins the wording, but which routes and files are obsolete is a review judgement no check can make.
Whether a close, done, supersede or status claim matches its sources is a judgement over issue text, comments and code; no script can read that meaning.

rows.rule: On "you are taking over as controller for <repo>"
rows.covers: The reconciler's takeover claim stops the old writer before its next write. The capability check and the journey are instruction-only.

rows.rule: Beneath explicit owner authority and platform instructions

instruction_only.why: Instruction precedence and what a session loads are read by the agent; no hook sees which instructions it followed.

rows.rule: An authorised in-gate refresh reads changed sources

instruction_only.why: The refresh notice and the choice not to restart happen inside the session; nothing outside it can check them.
What a return says is free text read by the controller; no schema checks it.

rows.rule: Routines/executors send findings and owner asks to the controller

instruction_only.why: Where a routine or executor sends a finding or owner ask is a judgement per message; the owner-post rule lives on the principles page.

rows.covers: The reconciler keeps each programme finding with its controller next action until it is answered, and the Projects daily check-in turns failing tasks, PRs that need a step and long-missing project tasks into first-line prefixes the coordinator must act on. Judging the action and deadline for any other finding is the controller's. The escape-list script writes one checked line for each bug found after merge and refuses a malformed line or one holding a local path, secret or personal data; deciding that a bug is an escape stays the controller's.

instruction_only.why: Native host controls hold standing authority; Toolkit code records none of it and cannot see uncertain effects.
instruction_only.probe: Check whether the host now exposes its permission grants to a hook or a command Toolkit can read (Claude Code permission settings, Codex approvals); if it does, record and compare them.

rows.covers: The merge hold and the auto-merge check stop merges without the owner's OK or a passing check. Deletions, keys and other irreversible steps are instruction-only.
The merge hold lets merges into an evidence store through without asking. Secret scans and the sole-copy rule are instruction-only.

rows.rule: These pages are part of this file
rows.covers: The pages check fails when a page is missing, unlisted, out of step with its hash or has a rule with two homes.
The pages check fails when this page is missing or its hash is stale.
The pages check fails when this page is missing or its hash is stale.
The pages check fails when this page is missing or its hash is stale.
The pages check fails when this page is missing or its hash is stale.

instruction_only.why: Ranking the principles above skills and briefs is a reading order; no check can tell when a brief relaxes one.
A pointer to the global Development Principles, which the controller applies by judgement in plans, reviews and merges.
A pointer that keeps governance-owned principles out of this page; the governance checks enforce those themselves.

rows.covers: The merge hold and the auto-merge check stop merges without the owner's OK or a passing check. Branch deletes and permission edits sit in the global rules and are instruction-only.

The attribution hook refuses a force push in a governed or guarded repository and to an evidence store, and AI attribution in commits; no history rewrite elsewhere and the owner's commit identity stay instruction-only.
The programme sweep raises POLISH_CAP for a polish child at 8 rows, above 8 rows or with two open. Filing a Low as a row, and fixing a one-line Low in the PR, stay judgement.

The programme sweep raises the net findings (finished children to judge, owner-OK closes, unexplained new children, closed parents with open children, unticked rows, full polish children and open pull requests no task in progress owns), and in Claude Code the turn-end owed check stops the controller's turn once for each new one due. Judging done, obsolete children, the same-day route of a flagged pull request and folding the owner's OK into the next ask stay judgement.

instruction_only.why: How the controller gets a capability it lacks is a per-harness judgement.
Spotting a clash between a harness skill and the local rules is a reading judgement.

Whether the owner started or agreed to a cloud start is read from the chat, and no Toolkit check reads a session start's target yet. A deferred or paused scheduled run is a controller decision; the Projects run check prints every run left pending.
Batch size and lane use stay a judgement; stacking a ready pull request onto an open merge train is code-decidable.
instruction_only.planned: #1030 S1: the train finder stacks onto an open train by default, and a separate build needs a reason.

instruction_only.why: What the owner needs to read, and the wording of each post, is a judgement.
Choosing plans and review routes is an owner-set limit, not something code can check.
A design principle the controller applies by judgement in plans, reviews and merges; what counts as an unasked mention is a wording call.

rows.covers: CI refuses a hooks.json with no harness, a hook command with no scope row or with a second command chained after its script, a hook on an event its row does not name and justify, a row naming a hard rule off the closed list, a script serving two harnesses, a module two harnesses load with no policy or library row or holding a harness's tool names, environment names or output fields, a require it cannot follow, and a known-open list that grows or keeps a clean item. Whether a rule really is a hard rule stays a controller and review judgement.

Gate assignments: each assign or reopen opens a gate session entry, and the sweep raises CLOSE_DUE once the assignment is finished with nothing owed until its close is recorded. In Claude Code the turn-end owed check stops the controller's turn once for each new CLOSE_DUE, each finished side session the desktop app shows unarchived, and each gate launch or archive with no gate-session record. Sessions on other hosts, and whether the final message was read in full and acted on, stay instruction text.
Stack selection resolves each role and the reviewer set only from the pinned registry, with no default or fallback.

rows.rule: Launch every gate with model and effort pinned explicitly
rows.covers: On Claude Code, the gate launch hook refuses a start_session gate brief without valid Gate, Route and Assignment lines or with an unpinned model or effort, and after a capped start prints the effort raise and record steps; the started session's route check refuses an off-pin gate. Projects threads and starts by a person stay instruction-only.

instruction_only.why: Gatekeepers are not used on Claude Code; on Projects or Codex no Toolkit launcher starts the gatekeeper, so its tier cannot be checked there.
instruction_only.probe: When Projects or Codex gatekeepers are used, test whether that host runs Toolkit's hooks on the gatekeeper's launch call or session start; if it does, check its tier there.

rows.covers: The merge-train script's verify lists the files two or more members change, so the controller sees when a train needs a delta review; a hand-resolved or edited merge fails verify, so a lane cannot fix a conflict inside the train. For route owner, land prints the merge step: the agent gives the effects and runs the exact merge, and the merge guard asks; it asks first only where no guard is known to run or task auto-merge would let the merge through unasked. The lane's model tier, skipping G0 and G1, and following that step stay instruction-only.

The helper guard checks a helper launch against its pinned route and refuses one that would launch another agent, when a host hook calls it; the depth setting keeps spawn depth at one. Reading run logs is instruction-only.

instruction_only.why: The service tier is chosen in the host when a session starts; Toolkit has no setting to check.
instruction_only.probe: Check whether start_session or the host's session metadata gains a service-tier field a hook can read.

rows.covers: Stack selection resolves the full reviewer set from the same selection. When G2 starts, fresh contexts and independence are instruction-only.

rows.rule: The owner may address G0/G1 directly

instruction_only.why: Whether a relay is faithful and which input is stale is read by the gate; no record carries it.

rows.covers: The reconciler records each child's gate state from its checkpoints and flags a stale or competing one. Reusing a session and consuming a return once are instruction-only.
The auto-merge check needs a UAT line on the pull request, and the reconciler records UAT retained, partial or full. Deciding which steps need owner UAT is instruction-only.

instruction_only.why: Whether a feature needs an invariant model is a G0 judgement that G2 checks by reading.

rows.covers: The decision history reads the SCOPE-CONFIRMED tag as the owner's confirmation of a child's scope. Asking the owner is instruction-only.

rows.rule: G2 tests scope, execution, security and evidence

instruction_only.why: Rating findings stays the reviewer's judgement; counting review rounds per pull request is code-decidable.
instruction_only.planned: #1030 L3: the train finder counts Toolkit-G2 verdicts per pull request and prints the round, and the cap rule on a third.

instruction_only.why: Readable text is judged by G1 and G2; the plain-reference check covers only issue and PR references in docs.

rows.covers: Evidence store writes go through toolkit-store.cjs save, which pushes the bound branch with a plain fast-forward push and reads it back with one fetch; the shell hooks refuse a raw push to a bound store. Minimal edits and readback for pull request and issue text stay instruction-only.

instruction_only.why: Whether work is finished is a judgement at the end of each turn.

rows.rule: Reuse the user-selected private evidence store
rows.covers: Governance discovery lists the owner's existing private evidence stores before proposing a new one, and a name alone selects nothing. Verifying access through the backend is instruction-only.
In a Git store, toolkit-store.cjs save commits, pushes and fetches once as the read-back, and the shell hooks refuse a raw push to a bound store; which files to archive at gate end stays a judgement.

instruction_only.why: Which worktrees and branches are safe to remove follows this rule's tests in the workspace residue report; removing them after a lane lands is code-decidable but not yet run by any step.
instruction_only.planned: #1225 S7: the merge train's land step prints the lane's safe removal lines, and the daily net raises WORKSPACE_RESIDUE for ready worktrees over a day old.

rows.covers: The merge-train script refuses a train that holds anything but member merges at their reviewed heads, clean main catch-up merges and one reproducible bump, and its land check refuses a moved main, a moved member head, a RISKY member with no owner OK, or a member whose live UAT line is missing, invalid or stricter than the manifest's. Its eject command takes a boarded member off a pushed train with recorded reverts only, which verify accepts exactly, and land refuses while an ejected pull request still points into the train. Verify, catchup and eject also refuse a train whose tree differs from a fresh build of its members on main, so no train merged onto the main land checked undoes merged work; governance's up-to-date check (P6) makes GitHub refuse a merge onto any other main. Stacking is the script's default: find writes onto while a train pull request is open, and build on main refuses beside an open train unless --separate gives a reason; a ready land lists the closing stories, sessions and worktrees owed after the merge. Choosing which PRs ride together, posting those stories and running the merge stay instruction-only.

instruction_only.why: Promises live in free text (PR, issue comments or project memory); the hourly nudge reads them, but no code parses them.
instruction_only.planned: #1225 L2: a structured promise with a trigger (PR merged, PASS, version) and a PROMISE_DUE sweep finding.

instruction_only.why: Which action fits a finding, and when a repeat or missed deadline needs the owner, is a judgement per finding; the check-in prefixes and programme attention that feed it are mapped on the core rule.
instruction_only.planned: #1225 S2: a turn-end check blocks once on findings due (new for 4 hours or acknowledged past due).

rows.rule: Native coverage: Codex/Claude Code on real selected paths

instruction_only.why: The rule itself says host qualification is not implemented. Install health checks only that installed copies, hooks and helper files are current, not the listed host behaviours.
instruction_only.probe: Run the real-host qualification matrix on each selected host; move this row to enforced when a qualification run records a result Toolkit checks.

rows.rule: **G0 Discovery** runs for every new task

instruction_only.why: Whether a task is new or a fix inside an already-discovered task, and how short discovery may be, is a planning judgement.

rows.rule: **G1 Builder** starts in a fresh session

instruction_only.why: Who owns an outcome, whether a fix is in scope and the builder's own diff self-check happen inside the builder's session.

rows.covers: The risk-tier script tags a change by its paths, and the train finder boards a pull request only with a G2 PASS for its head, at no lower tier than its paths give; which reviewers run stays the controller's.

rows.rule: are fine where the reader needs them

instruction_only.why: A wording allowance; there is nothing to check.

rows.rule: Fresh executor contexts are mandatory between G0 and G1

instruction_only.why: Whether a switch, compaction or replacement needs a fresh executor is read per run; no host record says when renewal is due.
Keeping work recoverable (pushed branches, current pull requests, posted decisions) is a habit checked by reading; the programme handover command records it but cannot judge it.

rows.rule: A gate works in the primary checkout unless it needs its own worktree

instruction_only.why: Whether a gate needs its own worktree is a per-gate call; removal after merge is covered by the scratch rule's row.
Whether behaviour has a cohesive owner object and honest effect order is a design review judgement.
Whether a feature needs a written model and closure matrix is a G0 judgement that G2 checks by reading.
Whether a reader is default-deny over its stated subset is a review reading; the hostile-input helper is a test tool, not a check.
Whether a repository has its own convention is read from that repository, and a branch name grants nothing, so a wrong name costs only a rename.
Which work is a ship blocker and which is post-ship is a judgement per change.

rows.rule: G1 checks the actual user or operator surface for clarity

instruction_only.why: Clear and safe text is judged by G1 and G2 reading it.

rows.rule: owed agent UAT starts at once
rows.covers: The pull request body pre-flight refuses an OWNER_TEST_NEEDED body without one `Agent UAT: PASSED (<evidence>)` line; starting agent UAT at once, in parallel with the lane, stays the controller's.
The merge check accepts an OWNER_TEST_NEEDED line, so owner UAT never holds a merge; recording UAT PENDING on each Refs task at merge stays the controller's.

instruction_only.why: CI cannot drive a fresh chat on an installed build, so the real-host smoke and qualification matrix run by hand once per release batch.
instruction_only.probe: Test whether a host offers a scripted fresh-chat run on the installed plugin (for example a headless Claude Code run with the installed build and its hooks) that can replay the smoke rows, with a positive control refusal in the same run.

rows.rule: A new SHA alone does not invalidate UAT
rows.covers: The programme state records UAT_RETAINED, UAT_PARTIAL_REQUIRED and UAT_FULL_REQUIRED, bound to a head; the impact evidence is the controller's.

rows.rule: G2 starts after the working result

instruction_only.why: Coverage, adversarial depth and rating findings are the reviewers' judgement; the train finder reads only each verdict's first line and route stamps.

rows.covers: For hooks, the pack's expectation check fails a pull request that removes, lowers or changes a row without a Pack changes reason; for other guard code the base-on-head run is the reviewer's.

instruction_only.why: Whether an early return skips a generic guard is a code review reading.

rows.rule: Before the first fix of a security finding

instruction_only.why: Listing every route to one invariant is a reviewer and builder analysis.

rows.rule: After a G2 PASS, a delta G2 runs
rows.covers: The train finder boards a pull request only with a PASS for its current head or a scripted carry, so an edit after a PASS needs a new verdict; whether an edit is RISKY or changes reviewed behaviour stays the reviewer's.

The review carry script accepts a carry only in its exact cases (a body-only FAIL with its Carry line, the shard bot's manifest refresh, sync outputs only), with the same files, green checks and valid UAT and Bump lines.

instruction_only.why: Which reviewers recheck, what a fix reaches and when a family closure record holds are reviewer judgements.
Whether a finding is on code no fix touched, and whether it is a proved High, is the reviewer's judgement.
Whether a finding is a proved High stays a judgement; counting Toolkit-G2 verdicts per pull request is code-decidable.
instruction_only.planned: #1030 L3: the train finder counts Toolkit-G2 verdicts per pull request and prints the round, and the cap rule on a third.

rows.covers: CI runs the hook pack on Linux and Windows on the exact head, and its expectation check needs a Pack changes reason for each removed, lowered or changed row; the revert proof is the builder's and the real-host smoke the controller's.

rows.rule: Gate models and effort come only from an explicitly selected stack registry
rows.covers: The gate route check reads each gate's pin from the selected stack registry and refuses a gate session off it; adopting a newer registry stays the controller's.

rows.rule: Model and effort follow launch ownership

instruction_only.why: Whether a session was opened by a human or launched by automation is read from the launch; the route check applies only to launcher-marked gate sessions.

rows.covers: The gate route check reads the host's launch record and refuses a gate session whose model or effort is inherited, missing or off its pin, and refuses a verdict or builder body with the wrong Route stamp.

rows.rule: Keep model, effort, tier and route out of portable task prompts

instruction_only.why: What a portable prompt needs and whether two builders' files are disjoint are judged per brief.

rows.covers: The merge hold reads task auto-merge only from a fresh, enabled, merged binding, and honours no label or per-app answer the binding does not hold.

rows.rule: With On, the controller, in a session the owner started, merges when
rows.covers: The auto-merge eligibility check exits non-zero for a head whose scope or UAT line does not qualify, and the merge hold checks the scope before a standing merge; recording G2 PASS, the other conditions and the notice after it stay the controller's.

rows.rule: That check exits 1 for bindings and their schemas/readers
rows.covers: The auto-merge eligibility check exits 1 for every listed path family and for a major bump, so those wait for the owner's typed merge.
